unresolved_should_improve.claim: The first draft kept a clause saying the Trusts were revolutionary and troubled all old conventions; the revision deletes it. The text now jumps from the Trusts representing new power straight to Adams as 'one of their earliest victims'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Battling Trusts' and the hysteria of p1 imply hostility.

evidence.quote: They were revolutionary, troubling all the old conventions and values, as the screws of ocean steamers must trouble a school of herring.
they were revolutionary, troubling all the old conventions and values.
The Trusts stood for the larger part of the new power that had been created since 1840. As one of their earliest victims, a citizen of Quincy

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the first draft's clause: '; they were revolutionary, troubling all the old conventions and values.'
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: The plan allows condensing the 'screws of ocean steamers' simile, not removing the claim itself.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The victimhood and the 'learned submission' argument lose their mechanism. Without it, sympathy with Roosevelt's battle reads as unmotivated.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Revision removes why Adams is a Trusts 'victim'

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The revision cuts 'The old one had plainly reached the end of his strength, and his failure had become catastrophic,' along with the 'ten times the endurance' specification. Both were present in the first draft.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Hysteria and the Diocletian parallel still convey crisis.

evidence.quote: for the old one had plainly reached the end of his strength, and his failure had become catastrophic.
The old one had plainly reached the end of his strength, and his failure had become catastrophic.
were demanding a new type of man. A traveller in the highways of history

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Reinstate the first draft's single sentence about the old one's failure.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: the plan lists 'the demand for a new type of man' as essential.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The new-man thread is an essential item that recurs in p2 ('produce the new man'). It now lacks its old-man counterpart and its measure of scale.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Demand for a new man loses its cause (the old man's collapse)

unresolved_should_improve.claim: The source introduces the umpire through both forces having been familiar since childhood without favoring him. It later explains that the umpire's attitude infuriates the players. Both are cut, so 'it was the umpire' arrives as an unannounced figure with an unexplained claim.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: Readers can infer that the umpire is Adams from 'a student of mechanics'.

evidence.quote: Both had been familiar since childhood, as the story has shown, and neither had warped the umpire's judgment by its favors.
Naturally such an attitude annoyed the players in the game, as the attitude of the umpire is apt to infuriate the spectators.
If ever judge had reason to be impartial, it was the umpire.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Prefix: 'Neither force had warped the umpire's judgment by its favors;'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: 'Adams as impartial umpire' is essential.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: Coming right after Adams calls himself the Trusts' victim, the impartiality claim reads as contradictory. The metaphor also loses its payoff.
unresolved_should_improve.title: 'The umpire' introduced without basis for impartiality

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Two cuts leave dangling references. 'Better' compared the theory to the uselessness of a nineteenth-century education, which is cut. 'There, the duty stopped' referred to pointing out economies for the new American's education, also cut. It now follows 'economize waste of mind', and the 'There, too, life stopped' chain rests on it.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Submission and silence' in p2 offers a loose antecedent for 'better reason'.

evidence.quote: a nineteenth-century education was as useless or misleading as an eighteenth-century education had been to the child of 1838; but Adams had a better reason
it pointed out the economies necessary for the education of the new American. There, the duty stopped.
it tended to encourage foresight and to economize waste of mind. There, the duty stopped.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the clause 'If it was not itself education, it pointed out the economies necessary for the education of the new American.' before the duty line.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: A planning omission: the residue of permitted compression is left dangling.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The hinge from argument to elegy becomes cryptic at the chapter's turning point.
unresolved_should_improve.title: 'A better reason' and 'the duty' lose antecedents

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Several details are cut: 'One has done it so often!', Hay's inability to pace the deck, his conviction he would not return, and his light talk of the death sentence. As a result, 'but' now oddly contrasts 'no illusions' with 'tasks incomplete'.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: The revival and the 'good-bye with a smile' survive.

evidence.quote: he talked lightly of the death sentence that he might any day expect, but he threw off the coloring of office and mortality together
Hay nourished no illusions, but the malaria of power left its only trace in the sense of tasks incomplete.
Hay nourished no illusions, but the malaria of power left its only trace in the sense of tasks incomplete.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Insert 'he talked lightly of the death sentence that he might any day expect,' and restore 'One has done it so often!'.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: the plan lists 'the farewell with a smile' as essential.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: The smiling-farewell aphorism floats, and Hay's joking acceptance of death is lost. That acceptance prepares the tone of 'I've not time!'
unresolved_should_improve.title: Hay's light fatalism on deck flattened

unresolved_should_improve.claim: Two cuts thin the ending. The comment that Shakespeare needed only the commonplace to express the inexpressible is gone, so the quotation stands bare. Also cut is 'scores of emperors and heroes fade into cheap obscurity', the stated reason Adams is satisfied for Hay.
unresolved_should_improve.counterevidence: 'Hamlet's Shakespearean silence' later attributes the quotation.

evidence.quote: Shakespeare himself could use no more than the commonplace to express what is incapable of expression.
One had seen scores of emperors and heroes fade into cheap obscurity even when alive; and now, at least, one had not that to fear for one's friend.
he was even satisfied to have his friend die in full fame, universally regretted, and wielding his power to the last.

unresolved_should_improve.minimal_repair: Restore the emperors sentence; optionally restore the Shakespeare commonplace sentence.
unresolved_should_improve.plan_relation: Required: the plan lists 'the rest is silence' and 'satisfied for Hay's sake' as essential.
unresolved_should_improve.reader_effect: This weakens the silence theme, which links V3 to the close. Adams's satisfaction also seems less reasoned and more callous.
unresolved_should_improve.title: Narrator's Shakespeare reflection and the emperors rationale cut
